answer: Independent history recall audit. Each identity must keep a private signed log of its own actions and answer random challenges by returning a quill-signed transcript within a deadline. Audits compare transcripts to the public ledger; clones sharing memory or replaying one log produce a detectable echo in timing and errors. Every identity also publishes a slow-growing vine of unique interactions, so fabricated histories must be maintained separately. An attacker pays per identity for distinct storage, compute, and failed-audit exclusion from payouts.
